heroHeadline: Senate Passes $70B ICE/CBP Funding Package 52-47 — Largest Immigration Enforcement Appropriation in U.S. History
heroSubtitle: In the early hours of June 5, 2026, the U.S. Senate passed a $70 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation package 52-47 after an approximately 19-hour vote-a-rama — the largest single congressional appropriation for ICE and CBP in U.S. history. Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) was the only Republican to vote against; no Democrat voted for it. The breakdown: ~$38.6B for ICE, $26B for CBP, and ~$5B in discretionary DHS enforcement funds, locked in through the rest of Trump's term and insulating both agencies from future government shutdowns. The $1.776B anti-weaponization settlement fund for Trump political allies survived all Democratic amendment attempts. The bill now goes to the House (in recess). On day four of his tenure, Acting ICE Director David Venturella — a former senior GEO Group executive — issued an internal memo on June 4 rescinding the 30-day post-release death reporting requirement, narrowing accountability as the agency records its most lethal year in history. On June 3, New Jersey AG Jennifer Davenport and Newark Mayor Ras Baraka separately filed lawsuits demanding inspection access and seeking closure of Delaney Hall; a DHS OIG report released the same day found Winn Correctional Center staff in Louisiana choked a detainee and stabbed another with a pen — ICE concurred with all 9 remediation recommendations. Human Rights Watch published a detailed report on Delaney Hall detainee conditions. An NPR investigation found GEO Group — which operates Delaney Hall — saw its annual profits surge nearly 700% in 2025 (from $32M to ~$254M) as ICE detention expanded.
